title: Tests repo: plant-products m4 pages + hub/CYA feature specs (the 12-spoke assurance)
recipe: No recipe. The script is SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §10.5 (Pages + Features rows), §2.1 (the 12-spoke → section → row → pages → obligations table, which this increment is the assurance for), §2.2 (39 pages accounted for), §3.1 (transport / goods-movement / contacts / documents / parties obligations) and FD-12 (the review section's authored gate).

EXTEND the flow to a COMPLETE, SUBMITTABLE notification: add `answerTransport`, `answerGoodsMovement`, `answerContact`, `answerNominatedContacts`, `answerDocuments`, `answerTraders`, `reviewAndSubmit`, plus a `completeMandatorySpokes()` convenience that walks every mandatory spoke and returns to the hub ready for review. Keep the fill/save/answer split.

`completeMandatorySpokes()` is what pp-065 and pp-066 both build on — get its granularity right here (each spoke independently callable, plus one call for all of them) and neither of those increments needs to reopen this file.

NEW — one spec per page landed above: `transport.spec.ts`, `goods-movement.spec.ts`, `contact.spec.ts`, `nominated-contacts.spec.ts`, `documents.spec.ts`, `traders.spec.ts`, `consignor.spec.ts`, `review.spec.ts`, `declaration.spec.ts`, `confirmation.spec.ts`.

EACH covers the same five things: renders with the right heading and fields; valid save returns to the hub and updates the row status; each mandatory field missing produces an error-summary entry LINKED to its field; the back link returns to the hub; a saved answer is present on re-entry (real backend resume). Persisted values assert through `plantProductsApi.load(ref)` as CODES/ENUMS, not labels.

Per-page specifics worth naming: `transport.spec.ts` must assert that changing the BCP CHANGES the available inspection premises (the allow-list is lazily resolved per gate execution — a cached option list is the defect); `goods-movement.spec.ts` must assert the MRN field is required only under ADD_MRN_NOW and NOT under the other two.

NEW — THE ASSURANCE FOR §2.1's 12-SPOKE MAPPING, and the direct mirror of the live-animals spec of the same name (`tests/e2e/features/live-animals/hub-groups-and-cya-rows.spec.ts`).

ASSERT:
1. Every spoke appears under the right numbered GROUP heading, in the order §2.1 gives: 1 Origin of the import, 2 Purpose, 3 Commodity, 4 Additional details, 5 Transport to the BCP, 6 Goods movement services, 7 Contact details, 8 Nominated contacts, 9 Accompanying documents, 10 Traders, 11 Billing, 12 Review and submit.
2. Each row's STATUS changes as its section is completed (Not started → In progress → Completed).
3. Spoke 8 (Nominated contacts) is OPTIONAL and does NOT gate readiness — leave it empty and still reach review.

5. Spoke 12 (Review and submit) is NOT a task row (FD-12) — it is the authored gate `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers` — and it unlocks ONLY when every mandatory row is Completed. Assert both states: locked with one mandatory row outstanding, unlocked when none is.
6. Every CYA row on the review page maps to a spoke, and its Change link returns to the page that owns the answer and then back to the review page.

ASSERT THE FULL RENDERED LIST, dividers and separators included — do not filter visual elements out of the option/row assertions to make them tidy.

NEW. Pins the c-015 floor: with ZERO accompanying documents the spoke-9 row is not Completed and review does not unlock; with ONE it is and it does. Also assert removing the last document takes it back to incomplete — a minEntries floor that only works on the way up is a common half-implementation.

notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. Verbatim scripts: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test": "npm run _assert_stack && npm run _clean && npm run database:reseed && npm run _test_e2e"; "test:local"; "test:a11y"; plus `test:plant-products` from pp-060.

THIS IS THE BIGGEST INCREMENT IN THE TESTS-REPO SET and it is deliberately not split: eleven pages, one flow completion and four feature specs. Splitting it would leave the flow half-complete, and a half-complete flow means pp-065's whole-journey spec, pp-066's a11y walks and pp-067's lifecycle seeds all block on a partial `completeMandatorySpokes()`. If it has to be broken up under time pressure, break it PAGE-WISE (pages + their per-page specs first, the four feature specs second) and never leave `journey.ts` unable to reach the review page.

WHY `hub-groups-and-cya-rows` IS THE ASSURANCE FOR §2.1: the 12-spoke mapping is a PLAN artefact — spoke → flow section → task row → pages → obligations file. Nothing in the frontend enforces that the built hub matches it; GROUPS is authored by hand in the hub controller. This spec is the only executable statement of the mapping, which is why it asserts order, grouping, status transitions, the optional row, the conditional row and the gate rather than just 'twelve rows are present'.

EVIDENCE STANDARD: assert the full rendered list including dividers and separators. Filtering visual elements out of an option or row assertion to make it read nicely hides exactly the regressions these specs exist to catch.

WHAT THIS REPO ADDS OVER THE FRONTEND'S OWN SPECS: real backend, real Mongo, real OIDC. So the wipe-on-gate-flip case in `containers-conditional`, the resume-after-save cases, and every persisted-code assertion are the point — the frontend's stub-backed specs cannot prove any of them.

DEPENDS ON pp-040 (the frontend m4 close). Do not start writing page objects against pages that have not landed; locate against the built pages.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.
openQuestions: Whether spoke 11 (Billing) is genuinely absent from the m4 hub or present-but-Not-applicable. Planned resolution: assert what the built hub renders and say which it is in the spec; the plan says `conditional: true` hides a Not-applicable row (§2.1, recipe §3.6), so absent is expected — but assert the observed behaviour, not the expected one, and flag a mismatch rather than accommodating it.

Whether `responsiblePerson*` is pre-populated at m4. Planned as NO (POP-2 auto-population is deferred with inc-032), so the specs enter the values by hand; if the built page arrives pre-filled, that is a plan/implementation divergence to flag, not to absorb into the spec.
